stories.title: Lee asks for unity in meeting with newly elected leadership of ruling party
stories.summary: President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday asked the new leadership of the ruling Democratic Party (DP) to enhance unity among party members, according to Cheong Wa Dae. Lee made the remarks at a dinner meeting with the party's new leadership, including the new DP leader Kim Min-seok. "I hope members of the DP could put aside their minor differences and devote themselves wholeheartedly to building a great Republic of Korea, which the people have entrusted us," Lee told the meeting, referring to South Korea by its official name, according to Cheong Wa Dae. Lee's remarks came amid lingering tensions exposed during the leadership race between those aligned with Lee and supporters of former DP leader Jung Chung-rae. Lee also asked the new leadership to provide policy support for the government and the presidential office, saying close cooperation between the three entities could help make palpable changes for the people.

stories.title: Mobilisation fears grip Russians as Kremlin's forced recruitment spikes
stories.summary: Human rights groups said they recorded a surge in forced recruitment since mid-August, amid reports that Russia is preparing a new mobilisation wave after September's elections. Russian security forces are detaining civilians off the streets and pressuring them to sign military contracts, as reports emerge that the Kremlin is preparing for a new wave of mobilisation for its ongoing all-out war in Ukraine. In mid-August, the Russian human rights project Idite lesom received 14 appeals from people who said security forces had detained them and forced or pressured them into signing military contracts, either at police stations or directly at military enlistment offices. The project, which helps Russians avoid taking part in the war, said the peak began on 10 August. "There were only isolated round-ups in July, now we are at a peak," Ivan Chuvilyaev, a representative of the project, told Euronews. Reported cases span from Novorossiysk to Birobidzhan. Men have been detained on the street under the pretext of document checks or for drinking in public, at their workplaces, and on their way home. Cases in the Penza region have been recorded since mid-June. In the same period, Idite lesom — whose name is a deliberate play on a Russian expression meaning "get lost" —reported seven cases of conscript soldiers being forced or pressured to sign contracts with the Russian Defence Ministry. Prison authorities are also being used as a recruitment channel. Chuvilyaev said representatives of Russia's Federal Penitentiary Service are searching for potential contract soldiers in remand centres and colonies. "If someone has money problems, the recruiters will find them," he said.

stories.title: China denounces US threat of sanctions over trade with Iran
stories.summary: Beijing says it will take ‘all necessary measures’ to protect its interests as US steps up efforts to isolate Tehran Explainer: could US sanctions threaten China-Iran ties? China has denounced the threat of US sanctions for its trade with Iran , saying any such measures would be illegal, and warned it will take “all necessary measures” to protect its national interests. Beijing’s rejection of the US threat of secondary sanctions for any country or entity continuing to trade with Tehran had been predicted. China buys an estimated 80% of Iran’s oil exports and it has defied previous US efforts to limit the flow of revenue to the Tehran regime. Continue reading...

stories.title: ‘The day I disclose, my career is over’: the journalist facing an $800 daily fine to keep her sources secret
stories.summary: If Catherine Herridge’s petition to the US supreme court fails, she’ll be on the hook for a daily fine until she discloses her sources – a case unsettling press freedom organizations For 18 days this summer, veteran journalist Catherine Herridge walked to her Washington DC mailbox and dropped off a check for $800. The money was required by law to cover a judge-imposed sanction after she was found in contempt of court in 2024 for refusing to disclose her sources. stories.title: Why Starlink won't open Vietnam's heavily censored internet
stories.summary: Starlink promises better connectivity in remote and mountainous areas. But in one of Southeast Asia's most tightly controlled online environments, more network access doesn't mean more free speech.
